sections.html:
Speed in Tyler comes down to three items: a buyer with no lender to wait on, clean title, and a payoff number that holds. Cash offers usually deliver all three more reliably than retail listings.

Start a folder with the mortgage payoff, your newest Smith County tax statement and any letter about a lien, code complaint or missed payment. Together they show what closing must clear and whether a deadline is already ticking.

  • Retail listing: wide exposure, plus showings, repair requests and a lender's calendar.
  • Private sale: price and terms are yours, along with every form.
  • Cash buyer: few contingencies, and the offer already prices in repairs.

Tyler is the Smith County seat, ninety-nine miles southeast of Dallas. Its townsite dates to 1846. Streets around the central square are old while subdivisions farther out are new, so houses range widely in age, and an inspector concentrates on whatever systems show a particular house's years.

Oil, roses, health care and education each shaped the city. Rose growing led to the Texas Rose Festival, held each October. Hospitals and four colleges, among them Tyler Junior College and the University of Texas at Tyler, tie housing demand to local jobs and campuses. A nurse relocating for a hospital post, a professor starting at a college, or a family moving from a smaller East Texas town all look at Tyler houses, and each weighs commute and school zone differently. Mention the features your own street offers when you talk to buyers.

Owned Tyler houses carry a typical value of $235,300 in the 2020-2024 estimates, and owners live in 55.4 percent of units. Individual houses land well above or below that mark.

Median household income is $67,486. About 85.7 percent of residents kept their address through the prior year, and most buyers come from nearby towns and from within Smith County itself.

Two separate offices matter. The appraisal district sets values and processes exemptions. The county tax office mails bills and accepts payment, but it plays no part in valuations, and the district is not county government. Take value questions to the district at 903-510-8600.

Payment options: walk in, pay online, mail a check to P.O. Box 2011, Tyler, Texas 75710, or use the drop box. The tax office phone is 903-590-2920. A card adds a 2.30 percent fee with a $1.50 minimum, and electronic checks are free. Noonday and Lindale substations accept payments as well. Current-year tax still open after January picks up penalty and interest on this schedule:

  • 7 percent in February, 9 in March, 11 in April, 13 in May and 15 in June.
  • 18 percent in July with a 15 percent collection fee added, then 19 in August and 20 in September.
  • Interest adds one percent each month, and whatever remains on June 30 passes to the delinquent tax attorney.

sections.h2: Proposed tax rates and the yearly calendar
sections.html:
Smith County runs a Truth in Taxes site for property owners. It shows property values, proposed tax rates, an estimate of the taxes those rates would produce, and the dates and places of public hearings on rates. Budget, revenue and rate calculations for taxing units are posted there too.

A Tyler address can be taxed by several units. County and school district levies hit every property, and some owners also pay a city plus a hospital, junior college, water or fire district. Elected boards for each unit set rates in August or September.

From January 1 to April 30 the appraisal district works through exemption applications and agricultural appraisals, and the review board begins hearing protests around May 15. Sellers should remember that late-summer rates decide the October bill. Your title company can explain how the year gets prorated between you and the buyer.

Your written protest must reach the district within 30 days of the date printed on the notice of appraised value. With no notice generated, May 20 is the fallback date. A letter naming you, identifying the property and showing you disagree is sufficient, and the online system works with the ID on your notice.

The district's taxpayer liaison officer can explain the process at 903-510-8600. A review board of citizens hears the protest, and you and the district exchange evidence at or before the hearing. Bring photographs, repair estimates and recent sales of similar houses, since the board weighs evidence rather than opinion.

Losing at the board leaves appeal routes: state district court, binding arbitration or the State Office of Administrative Hearings. A deadline on a weekend or holiday moves to the next working day. Only good cause, such as a medical emergency, excuses a late filing.

Taxable value on a qualifying homestead cannot rise beyond 110 percent of the prior year's value. In the first year an owner qualifies there is no cap, so a buyer begins uncapped. Owners 65 or older get a school tax ceiling fixed at what they paid in the year they first qualified. The ceiling can rise when they add improvements such as a room, a pool or a garage, and it changes if they move.

School districts also apply a $140,000 homestead exemption under state law. Pick up an application at the district office, 245 SSE Loop 323 in Tyler, weekdays from 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., or call 903-510-8600.

sections.h2: What happens between offer and closing
sections.html:
Once you say yes, a title company in Tyler opens a file and searches the property history for liens, judgments, unpaid taxes and gaps in ownership. A problem found now can be cured or priced in. A problem found the week of closing usually cannot.

Your buyer may tour the house. A cash buyer rarely asks you to fix what shows up on that visit. Next come a signing appointment with a notary and the payoff of your loan and any tax balance from the proceeds, with the rest going to you. Keys change hands at funding, so empty the house and schedule your utility shutoff a few days ahead.

sections.h2: Selling with taxes owed or an open estate
sections.html:
A tax balance does not stop a sale. At closing the title company settles it from your proceeds, working from a payoff the tax office confirms through your closing date. An estate still in probate adds a step, because the signer needs authority: a personal representative after appointment, or a route through a muniment of title or recorded transfer on death deed.

On your first title company call, have the death certificate, any will and the latest tax statement in hand, and ask what else is required. Settling that early protects your closing date once a buyer signs. After closing the deed is recorded with the Smith County Clerk, and your title company normally files it for you. Keep the recorded copy with your papers.

faqs.q: Which office handles a Tyler valuation complaint?
faqs.a: Phone the appraisal district at 903-510-8600. The county tax office has no role in valuations.

faqs.q: Where can I pay Tyler property tax?
faqs.a: Walk in at the county tax office, pay online or by mail, use the drop box, or stop at the Noonday or Lindale substation. Cards bring a convenience fee and electronic checks do not.

faqs.q: What happens if Tyler taxes go unpaid after January 31?
faqs.a: Penalty and interest begin at 7 percent in February and climb each month. Past June 30 the delinquent tax attorney takes over and a collection fee applies.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to protest a Tyler value?
faqs.a: Within 30 days of the date on your notice of appraised value, or May 20 if no notice went out. The notice itself prints your deadline.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Tyler house while a parent's estate is still open?
faqs.a: Only once someone holds authority to sign, such as an appointed personal representative or an heir using a muniment of title or recorded transfer on death deed. Ask a title company which papers it wants.
